They want 120 combined by the end of the break, so they still need 120 - 48 = 72 more signatures over the remaining 3 weeks. Daphne's average weekly rate during the first 3 weeks was 17/3 signatures per week. Since she now only collects on weekends, her weekly amount drops by 5 compared to the previous week, for each of the 3 remaining weeks: week1 = 17/3 - 5 = 2/3; week2 = 2/3 - 5 = -13/3; week3 = -13/3 - 5 = -28/3. Summing these gives Daphne's total contribution over the 3 remaining weeks: 2/3 + (-13/3) + (-28/3) = -39/3 = -13. So Olivia must supply 72 - (-13) = 85 signatures over the 3 remaining weeks, i.e., 85/3 ≈ 28.33 signatures per week.

inspection.overall_summary: No genuine Reasoning Drift was observed in this batch. Two problems (451, 458 — the popcorn-popping 4/5-stage sequential problems) were fully correct end-to-end with no errors of any kind. The two problems that produced wrong answers (271, 272 — the sisters'-signature-collection problems) both fail via Compositional Collapse rather than Reasoning Drift: in both cases the early bookkeeping (combined signatures so far, amount still needed) is correct, but the very next required structural piece — modeling how the declining collector's weekly rate behaves over the remaining weeks — is misconstructed from its first application in an identical, templated way across both problems (deriving a fractional 3-week 'average' and then recursively subtracting the weekly decrease). This is not a one-off numeric slip that then gets faithfully propagated; it is a wholesale wrong model of that stage, most starkly evidenced in idx 271 where the chain produces physically impossible NEGATIVE weekly signature counts (2/3, -13/3, -28/3), which could never occur if the model had gotten the recurrence's structure right and merely mis-added or mis-carried a number. Because the same broken rate-decline template is reused verbatim in idx 272 (with a different, still-wrong outcome relative to ground truth), this points to a systematic structural misunderstanding of that problem stage rather than an isolated arithmetic slip — the hallmark of Compositional Collapse, not Reasoning Drift.
